submission:
Root cause: No root cause was established. Six of seven dispatches returned tool failures or non-existent series rather than observations: both change-history queries died on a payload parse error at the 10,000-character boundary [tr_99e786adb0bd, tr_743335484daa], both log queries were rejected by Loki with HTTP 400 due to an invalid escaped-hyphen pod regex that was never corrected [tr_3644135888c3, tr_4f0bef88fe0e], and the span-metric error ratios for product-catalog and frontend were empty in incident and baseline windows alike, meaning the series does not exist rather than having dropped at onset [tr_bad85b91580f, tr_e35679d06e1f]. The only substantive signal is the trace sample [tr_d40c56f3c0c4], and it points away from product-catalog: its server spans finish in 0.8-9.3ms with sub-2ms postgresql children and no error status, and the frontend->product-catalog hop is clean on both sides. The 0.8-2.2s user-facing latency sits almost entirely in load-generator client GET self time, with the whole frontend+product-catalog subtree occupying ~3-21ms at the tail of each trace - an un-instrumented wait on the load-generator->frontend edge. On this evidence the failing mechanism cannot be named.
Faulty component: frontend
Fault type: unknown
Confidence: low

Evidence:
- Across the five sampled traces (71 spans total, 20 traces matched), no product-catalog span carries an error status; the only span marked ERROR is a load-generator client POST span in trace 0ac69139302ae5fe, which has no product-catalog descendant. (found, from trace_query on product-catalog)
- The result rendering exposes no span-level error attributes (no exception type/message/status description fields are surfaced for any span), so the specific error attributes on any failing product-catalog span cannot be read from this evidence. (found, from trace_query on product-catalog)
- product-catalog server spans (GetProduct, ListProducts) complete in roughly 0.8ms to 9.3ms, and each has a postgresql child span of 0.5ms to 1.6ms, so the datastore callee is fast and is not holding the parent open. (found, from trace_query on product-catalog)
- Where product-catalog GetProduct spans are slowest (~7-8ms self time in traces f81dd95288f4233a and 29f9fe76fd4a3cf1), the time is local self time rather than time spent in the postgresql child, indicating in-process work or scheduling delay inside product-catalog. (found, from trace_query on product-catalog)
- Overall trace latency of 0.8-2.2s is attributed by the degrading-hop analysis to load-generator client GET self time (100% of trace in four of five traces), with the entire frontend-to-product-catalog subtree occupying only ~3-21ms at the tail of each trace. (found, from trace_query on product-catalog)
- Evidence is partial: only 5 of 20 matching traces were shown and the result is marked truncated, so rare failing product-catalog spans could exist outside this sample. (found, from trace_query on product-catalog)
- product-catalog spans are failing and the failure was inherited from its postgresql callee (a database error propagating up). (ruled_out, from trace_query on product-catalog; why: Every postgresql child span in the sample completed normally in under 2ms with no error marking, and no product-catalog parent span is marked ERROR, so there is no callee-to-caller error propagation visible.)
- The ERROR observed in the window originates inside the product-catalog request path. (ruled_out, from trace_query on product-catalog; why: The single ERROR span is a load-generator client POST with no child spans and no product-catalog descendant; it sits on a sibling branch from the product-catalog GET branch, which completed cleanly in the same trace.)
- Multi-second user-facing latency is caused by slow product-catalog or its database. (ruled_out, from trace_query on product-catalog; why: In the four slow traces, the product-catalog subtree accounts for single-digit to low-double-digit milliseconds at the very end of the trace while the load-generator client GET self time accounts for essentially the whole duration.)
- The frontend is failing calls into product-catalog (timeouts or aborted gRPC calls at the frontend->product-catalog hop). (ruled_out, from trace_query on product-catalog; why: Every frontend GetProduct/ListProducts client span in the sample has a matching completed product-catalog server child and no error marking on either side of the hop.)
- The error-ratio query for product-catalog returned no samples in either the incident window or the preceding baseline window, so request rate, status-code breakdown, and latency percentiles cannot be derived from span-derived call metrics for this service. (found, from metric_baseline on product-catalog; query: sum by(service_name) (rate(traces_span_metrics_calls_total{service_name="product-catalog",status_code="STATUS_CODE_ERROR"}[5m])) / sum by(service_name) (rate(traces_span_metrics_calls_total{service_name="product-catalog"}[5m])))
- The absence spans both windows equally, which points to the span-metrics series for this service never existing in the queried backend rather than data disappearing at incident onset. (found, from metric_baseline on product-catalog; query: sum by(service_name) (rate(traces_span_metrics_calls_total{service_name="product-catalog",status_code="STATUS_CODE_ERROR"}[5m])) / sum by(service_name) (rate(traces_span_metrics_calls_total{service_name="product-catalog"}[5m])))
- product-catalog began emitting a surge of error-status spans around 02:26:33 that would show as a measurable error-ratio departure (ruled_out, from metric_baseline on product-catalog; why: The query covering the incident window returned no samples at all, so no error-ratio departure is observable on this signal; the hypothesis cannot be supported from span metrics and must be tested with logs or traces instead.; query: sum by(service_name) (rate(traces_span_metrics_calls_total{service_name="product-catalog",status_code="STATUS_CODE_ERROR"}[5m])) / sum by(service_name) (rate(traces_span_metrics_calls_total{service_name="product-catalog"}[5m])))

- This metric check confirms product-catalog was healthy during the window (ruled_out, from metric_baseline on product-catalog; why: An empty result is not a clean signal; the tool's own 'no sustained departure' phrasing follows from having nothing to compare, so health cannot be inferred.; query: sum by(service_name) (rate(traces_span_metrics_calls_total{service_name="product-catalog",status_code="STATUS_CODE_ERROR"}[5m])) / sum by(service_name) (rate(traces_span_metrics_calls_total{service_name="product-catalog"}[5m])))

Reasoning:
The trace sample actively excludes the obvious candidates: no callee-propagated database failure (postgresql children all under 2ms, unmarked), no failing frontend->product-catalog hop (every client span has a matching completed server child), and product-catalog's subtree is milliseconds at the end of multi-second traces [tr_d40c56f3c0c4]. What remains is a seconds-long wait accruing in the caller before the frontend server span starts, so the frontend is the service named - but whether it is slow to accept connections, briefly unreachable, or whether the load generator itself is the stall cannot be separated. The channels that would separate them all failed: product-catalog logs were never read [tr_3644135888c3, tr_4f0bef88fe0e], change history was never read and the second query's window started at onset and ran forward [tr_743335484daa], and the metric channel can support neither a spike nor health [tr_bad85b91580f, tr_e35679d06e1f]. Naming bad_config, bad_deploy or feature_flag would mean inventing a mechanism from a change log nobody successfully read.

Alternatives considered:
1. frontend: frontend is saturated (threads, connections, or CPU) and callers queue before their requests are accepted, producing caller-side self time with fast downstream spans. (resource_exhaustion). Ranked lower because: Fits the trace shape, but no frontend resource metric, log line, or pod state was ever collected; the only frontend dispatch returned a non-existent metric series [tr_e35679d06e1f].
2. load-generator: The load generator itself is the bottleneck (client-side contention or deliberate pacing), and no production service is faulty. (resource_exhaustion). Ranked lower because: Would explain 100%-self-time client spans and the lone orphan ERROR POST span, but load-generator was never dispatched against, and a critical multi-service alert is unlikely to be purely synthetic.

Open questions:
- What product-catalog and frontend logged at onset - the Loki query must be reissued with a valid matcher (pod=~"product-catalog-.*") before silence, exceptions, or flag text can be claimed.
- What changed before 02:26:33 - both change queries failed, and one used a window starting at onset running forward, so it could not have answered even on success; re-run backward with pagination.
- Where the load-generator client GET self time is actually spent: connection setup, frontend accept backlog, or load-generator-side scheduling - no frontend-side logs, resource metrics, or ingress data were gathered.
